changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 6 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/8653-listview-title-retired-rowactiondefs-pinned.md`

- names `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` → `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `title` — **retired.** `ListView` resolved its export filename through `schema.label || (schema as any).title`. `@objectstack/spec/ui`'s `ListViewSchema` refuses `title` **by name** (`unrecognized_keys: ['title']`) while `ObjectGridPropsSchema` **accepts** it; `packages/types` mirrors the platform contract rather than ruling over it, so declaring `title` on `ListViewSchema` would have made this repo accept what the platform save gate rejects. That asymmetry is also why objectui#6639 could take the *declare* branch for `ObjectGridSchema.title` one package over and this site could not. A parse-based census of `apps/ examples/ content/` and `packages/` found **zero** `list-view` nodes authoring `title`, so the retirement costs no author a filename. Over that same corpus the instrument reports **three** `object-grid` nodes carrying the key: **two authored** ones, both in `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md`, plus one that is not authored at all — `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` composes `title: schema.table?.title` onto a grid node it builds, so it is a producer writing the key rather than an author declaring it. `ObjectGrid`'s own `title` reads are untouched — they remain declared, ruled and read.

### `.changeset/object-view-unmirrored-keys-7779.md`

- names `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` → `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **What was measured.** Every reading was taken on the `object-view` node renderer (`packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx`, registered by `plugin-view/src/index.tsx`) with `schema.objectName` / `schema.layout` as the positive controls of the same `schema.KEY` query, so each zero is a reading; the repo-wide census of `viewTabBar` finds the key in no source file outside `@object-ui/types` (two doc tables listed it as authorable and are corrected here). The spec side was read through the installed pin (`@objectstack/spec@17.2.0`, `ui` entry, 117 exported object schemas walked; control keys `objectName` / `columns` / `navigation` / `listViews` hit): the three spec-modelled keys are optional slots on `ListViewSchema` and `ObjectListViewSchema`; the six local keys have no spec slot anywhere.

- names `object-view-unmirrored-keys-7779.test.ts` → `packages/types/src/__tests__/object-view-unmirrored-keys-7779.test.ts` — edited by this change

  > ⚠️ **Dated note, 2026-09-28 — the value type has since been decided, and `listViews` is mirrored by reference — objectui#7928.** Later in this same release the maintainer's ruling A made `ObjectViewSchema.listViews` the protocol's own named-view record, by reference: on both faces its value is `@objectstack/spec`'s strict `ObjectListViewSchema`, and a `NamedListView` is not assignable to it. The docs have taught that shape since objectui#8255. So "`listViews` stays unmirrored", "The declaration's value is the local `NamedListView`", the key "stays in the parity ledger … until the maintainer decides its value type" and the table's "still unmirrored" above no longer hold: the `ObjectViewSchema` entry has left `UnmirroredDeclared`. `NamedListView` stays exported with its 64 declared members. The renderer reads some of them off a named view and leaves the rest unread, and the split is no longer the 21 and 43 this entry counted: objectui#7928 stopped reading the `options` bag, which the record refuses, and objectui#10758 made the host delegation read a named view's remaining protocol members off the named view. The census in `object-view-unmirrored-keys-7779.test.ts` pins the current figures. `.changeset/7928-listviews-by-reference-fold.md` (PR objectui#10821) states what ships; the text above is kept as the reading of this change.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `328abeb55` (merge-base with origin/main): 8 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1689 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2289 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36420601798)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `600cf89017790f5d8cde7296836db6be1c2a5300`

### ① Derived judgments

**The code is sound. The prose needs five fixes (listed at the end of this section).**

**`navigation`**
- **What the fence hands `ListView`.** It passes `navigation: currentNamedViewConfig?.navigation ?? activeView?.navigation ?? (schema as any).navigation`. That is three rungs, each taking the whole object. I re-derived both fence sha1s and they match the dev's at base and head (`40bc2292…` and `a140d042…`), so the fence is byte-identical.
- **Which navigation the delegation's row click follows.** It follows the named view when that view declares `navigation`, and the node otherwise. It never follows the `activeView`.
  - `ListView`'s `useNavigationOverlay` calls the `onRowClick` it is handed and then returns, so `ListView`'s own overlay never opens. `ObjectView`'s `formLayout` is the only record surface, and for a named view the handler and the relay now agree.
  - They still disagree in one case: a host `views` entry carries `navigation` and the named view does not. The relay then carries the `activeView` value and the handler the node's. This predates the PR, and the order forbids an `activeView` rung.
  - This case has no in-tree reach. The console passes its own `onRowClick` and no `listViews`, and no in-tree host passes both `listViews` and `renderListView`.
- **Whole-object replacement is correct.**
  - In the spec, `NavigationConfigSchema` is a strict object whose keys all have defaults (`mode` defaults to `page`; `preventNavigation` and `openNewTab` to false). A named view's `navigation` is `.optional()`. So a parsed named `navigation` is always complete, and a per-key merge could not mean anything.
  - The fence and `useNavigationOverlay` both take the whole object. Nothing merges key by key.
  - The whole-object pin tells a replacement apart from a merge: the node's `preventNavigation` would survive a merge.
- **Consumers of `navigationConfig`.** They are the `handleRowClick` branches (`none`/`preventNavigation`, `new_window`/`openNewTab`, `drawer`, `modal`, `page`, `split`/`popover`), `formWidthClass`, `formLayout` and the `NavigationOverlay` `width`. None of them has to stay node-level. But `formLayout` is also the container for the create and edit forms, because `handleCreate` and `handleEdit` open the same `isFormOpen` state. The PR discloses none of the following:
  - A named `navigation.mode` now also moves the New and Edit forms onto its surface. `split` swaps the whole tree `ObjectView` returns.
  - Under a named `split` or `popover`, the New button opens nothing.
    - The split branch draws the overlay only when `selectedRecord` is set, the popover branch requires it too, and `handleCreate` sets it to null.
    - This defect already exists for the node's own `navigation`. It is now reachable from a named view on route 2, where authored nodes show New by default. The Studio is not affected, because `ViewPreview` sets `showCreate: false`.
    - A code fix belongs on a follow-up card; the seat should file one.
  - A named `navigation` also turns on row clicks under a node's `operations.read: false`. The handler checks `operations.read` only when there is no navigation config. This matches how the node's own `navigation` behaves, and the docs already carry the "without a `navigation` config" qualifier.
- **Memo stability.**
  - With no named view active, `navigationConfig` is `schema.navigation` by reference, the same as base.
  - `currentNamedViewConfig` is memoized on `[hasNamedViews, activeNamedView, namedListViews]`, so `handleRowClick` is rebuilt only on a real switch. `gridSchema` does not depend on it.

**`inlineEdit` → `editable`**
- **`editable` is the right member.** `ObjectGridSlotKey` declares it, and `ListView` makes the same mapping (`editable: inlineEdit && inlineEditOffered`).
- **The gate, read in `ObjectGrid`.** `inlineEditable = (schema.editable ?? false) && objectInlineEditable`. `objectInlineEditable` is `isObjectInlineEditable(objectSchema, effectiveApiOps)` AND `perms.can(objectName, 'update')`. It feeds `editable`, `renderCellEditor` and the save column, so a named `inlineEdit` cannot widen editing past a grant.
- **Other sources of `editable` / `inlineEdit`:**
  - **The node's own `inlineEdit`.** It is one of the objectui#5097 host-composition keys (`OBJECT_VIEW_HOST_COMPOSITION_KEYS`), and objectui#5248 forbids reading those outside the fence. So having no node rung is required, not a gap. The code comment gives the weaker reason ("Route 2 handed the grid no `editable` before"); naming the host-composition reason instead is an optional tightening.
  - **`activeView`.** The registered renderer passes no `views`, and member 1's named-member block has no `activeView` rung.
  - **`table.editable`.** It is a declared `ObjectViewSchema.table` member that route 2 has never read, at base or at head. This PR does not shadow it. It is a declared-but-unenforced key sitting next to the new rung, and a candidate for a follow-up.
  - **The delegation's other rungs.** Its `activeView` and node rungs are reachable only through host composition, so the PR does not need to disclose the difference.

**`fieldOrder`**
- **`inFieldOrder` copies `ListView.effectiveFields` step for step.**
  - Same `columnIdentity` from `@object-ui/core`, the same rank `Map` and the same `?? Infinity` subtraction comparator. `Infinity − Infinity` is NaN, which Array sort treats as 0, so unnamed and identity-less entries keep their relative order on both routes.
  - Both apply it after `hiddenFields`. A name the projection does not carry orders nothing. With no projection it returns undefined, and `ListView` then hands its grid no columns. Both slots are ordered.
  - The only differences are an `Array.isArray` guard (stricter, harmless) and no field-level-security step. FLS belongs to `ObjectGrid` and does not affect order.
- **The parity pin drives both real routes.** It mounts route 2 of the real `ObjectView`, with the `ObjectGrid` export mocked as a sink, and the real `ListView` through `renderListView`, with the registry's `object-grid` as a sink. It is not a reimplementation.
- **The member-1 divergence is not made worse.** The set of kept and dropped identity-less entries is unchanged. Where route 2 keeps such an entry, it now sorts last.

**The objectui#7779 `READ_TEXT` edit**
- The edit is one `READ_TEXT` line plus a two-line comment. No figure moved.
- `navigation`, `fieldOrder` and `inlineEdit` were already in the whole-file read set through the fence, so the census stays at 43 read / 21 unread of 64 by reading.
